_comment: Generated by tools/m0-probes/probe2-emit-data.py from a real RetroBat install. Shape follows grout cfw/*/data/save_directories.json. Keyed by RetroBat system folder, not RomM slug; the slug join lives in the platform map. Paths are relative to <retrobat root>/saves/ and contain no absolute component.
_provenance: observed = seen on disk; declared = from es_savestates.cfg or es_features.cfg, not yet seen written

_classes.D: one container shared by many games

_note: Shape is a property of (system, emulator), not of system alone. psx is the worked example: libretro writes class A .srm, DuckStation writes memcards.

dreamcast.evidence: flycast/vmu/vmu_save_<PORT>1.bin shared by all games; convertible via flycast_vmupergame, port 1 only

per_game_conversion.note: driven: produces vmu/<SERIAL>_vmu_save_A1.bin (T40217N for Bangai-O), not a rom-named file, so it needs game-id attribution like class C. Port 1 only; ports B, C and D stay shared

gamecube.evidence: GCI folder under dolphin-emu/User/GC/<REGION>/, several .gci per game, .gci.deleted must be excluded

per_game_conversion.note: already the stock default; still needs attribution because .gci names carry the game code, not the filename

unit_paths.evidence: the * is the region subdirectory. 69-GXBE-game1.ssx.gci and 69-GXBE-settings.ssx.gci are one unit under key GXBE, and two .gci.deleted files sit beside live ones and must not travel

gamegear.evidence: loose .srm per rom, libretro genesis_plus_gx; path declared by the emulator, cart untouched in the run

mame.evidence: nvram/<shortname>/ where shortname is the rom basename, so attribution is by filename

unit_paths.evidence: 1231 unit directories, 1531 files, 137.3 MB, 8.02 s for the whole tree. The short name is the rom basename, so this is the one class C system needing no game-id attribution. Unprovable on the measured install, which holds 3 mame roms against 1231 units (measurement 153)

mastersystem.evidence: loose .srm per rom, libretro genesis_plus_gx; written at boot before any player save

megacd.evidence: per-rom .brm and .srm, plus a shared 4Mbit_cart.brm RAM cart

ps2.evidence: shared Mcd001.ps2 by default; convertible via pcsx2_slot1_memory=game

per_game_conversion.note: driven end to end on a real install: the card is '<rom stem>.ps2', so the extension is replaced and not appended, and it lands three levels deep under saves/ps2/pcsx2/memcards/ rather than loose. The stem is exactly the (folder, stem) key class A attribution already uses, so it needs no new route. The shared Mcd001.ps2 stops being written entirely, and console slot 2 stays shared. The third declared choice, 'folder', is NOT measured: whether it is per-game or a different container format for a still-shared card is unknown.

ps3.evidence: rpcs3/dev_hdd0/**/savedata keyed by TITLEID; 32k+ files, hashing is expensive

unit_paths.evidence: 77 files, 16.3 MB, 0.06 s, against 32451 files and 426.07 s for the rpcs3 data root above it. BLUS30109 owns three directories and BCUS98111 owns two. dev_hdd0/savedata is NOT declared: it held only an empty vmc directory and nothing measured says it is a save

psp.evidence: SAVEDATA/<GAMEID>/ containing PARAM.SFO, keyed by game id not filename

unit_paths.evidence: UCES01011 and ULES01513SYSDATA measured side by side, so the key is a prefix and one game can own several directories. PARAM.SFO adds nothing the directory name does not (measurement 144)

psx.evidence: loose .srm when libretro is selected; DuckStation instead writes memcards/<saveName minus disc>_<slot>.mcd, see shape_depends_on_emulator

per_game_conversion.keys_by: gamedb saveName with the disc marker removed, not the rom filename
per_game_conversion.note: Stock PerGameTitle binds a multi-disc set through DuckStation's own database, with or without a .m3u: a foldered two-disc set and a loose three-disc set each produced one card, named '<saveName minus disc>_<slot>.mcd'. The slot suffix is not a disc number and how many slots appear depends on the game. Regions stay separate because saveName carries them; revisions share a serial and a card. Save states are keyed on the rom file instead, so they are per disc while the card is per set. Not measured: the 130 stems keeping a subtitle behind the disc marker

wii.evidence: NAND tree under dolphin-emu/User/Wii/title/, mixed with non-per-game system state

unit_paths.evidence: the disc-game title tree. 52534245 decodes to RSBE and 524d4745 to RMGE. Only data/ travels: a title holding content/title.tmd with no data/ is an installed stub rather than a save. title/00000001 is system titles and shared2/, sys/ and fst.bin are system state, so none is declared

xbox.evidence: eeprom.bin and xbox_hdd.qcow2, a whole disk image shared by every game

_unit_paths._comment: Where a class C save unit lives, added in M6 stage 2b from a read-only sweep of a real install. A unit is a (container, key) pair and NOT a directory: ps3 keeps three directories under one title id and gamecube keeps two files and no directory at all (measurements 140 and 141). Paths are relative to <retrobat root>/saves/ and contain no absolute component. A '*' matches exactly one path segment. Anything no container names is reported unknown and never read, so a shape that named an emulator data root would cost 426 s per sync (142) and no shape names one.

_key_kinds.title_id: the entry is a directory and the key is a leading 4-letter 5-digit title id; the rest of the segment is the game's own suffix (UCES01011 bare, ULES01513SYSDATA suffixed, BLUS30187GAMEDAT9ZLDR0F5K7M4000)
_key_kinds.name: the entry is a directory and the key is the whole segment (mame short names)
_key_kinds.gci: the entry is a file named <makercode>-<gamecode>-<internal>.gci and the key is the game code; a soft-deleted .gci.deleted does not match and is excluded by construction rather than by a suffix list
_key_kinds.hex_ascii: the entry is a directory whose 8 hex characters decode to a 4-character ASCII game code (52534245 -> RSBE), which is the same code the .rvz header carries at 0x58

_unit_paths._slot_note: slot is declared rather than derived because it has to be stable forever and two containers on one system can end in the same segment. It becomes {emulator}:{slot}.
